defects.summary: Backfill is not idempotent and does not terminate: the batch selector has no WHERE retention_hours IS NULL guard, so after all rows are set the next batch reselects the same first 1000 rows, overwrites them, and never reaches zero rowcount (infinite loop; repeated overwrites of already-set values).
defects.trigger: backfill() selects rows by id LIMIT without filtering on retention_hours IS NULL; the stop condition is an UPDATE affecting zero rows, which never occurs.
defects.consequence: The backfill daemon loops forever and repeatedly rewrites rows, violating idempotence and blocking the migration completion signal.
defects.smallest_correction: Add WHERE retention_hours IS NULL to the UPDATE and select only still-NULL ids (idempotent and terminating).

defects.summary: Rollback destructively drops the column, losing backfilled retention_hours values and any data written to the new column, violating the 'no destructive step; rollback must not lose data for existing columns' constraint.
defects.trigger: rollback() runs ALTER TABLE jobs DROP COLUMN retention_hours.
defects.consequence: Rollback after partial or full backfill loses data.
defects.smallest_correction: Keep an additive rollback (additive column stays; backfill writes are restorable) and never drop the column without an explicit data-loss decision.

false_positive_pool.summary: Suggest adding an index on jobs.id to speed up the batch select.
